title: Founder charter-oath compact structure
scope: Qualitative charter-oath assembly balance mechanism of the settlement's standing founder-council compact; names, oath and law-code text, office counts, procedures, succession outcomes, candidates, faction rosters, ownership regimes, and fishing or harvest law remain open, and the first-succession provisions stay incompletely specified by design.
approval_evidence: On 2026-08-17 the Author selected 'C — Charter-oath assembly' in the explicit multiple-choice review of the founder-council compact proposal, accepting Option C exactly as drafted together with the proposal's shared claim set.
question: What qualitative balance mechanism should govern the settlement's standing founder-council compact — which office classes each side holds, which decision classes need which side or both, where refugee and newcomer representation enters, how craft, harvest, defence, and System-study expertise gets a voice, and which ambiguity classes the compact is known to contain — without choosing names, law-code text, succession outcomes or candidates, faction rosters, ownership regimes, or fishing and harvest law, and with first-succession rules staying incompletely specified by design?
selection: Use C — Charter-oath assembly, exactly as drafted, together with the proposal's option-independent shared claim set. The compact rests on a binding founding oath the founder swore in the founding era: the oath defines the dynasty's duties (defence, outward dealings, upholding the compact) and its limits (no burden without consent, no seizure of households' subsistence, no altering the compact alone). The council is chosen by an assembly of the settlement's households and holds two powers: it adjudicates disputes over whether the oath has been kept, and its consent is required for communal burdens. The dynasty's authority is real and broad within the oath's bounds; the council's is real because it judges those bounds and holds consent. Expertise enters as sworn craft, harvest, defence, and System-study testimony, with System-study testimony interpreting accessible signs and never a guaranteed readout. Whether the oath binds heirs automatically, only upon re-swearing, or lapses with the founder is unresolved, and the oath's terms are partly disputed recollection; that first-succession ambiguity is a designed open pressure cited by WLD-EVENT-001 and is never resolved here.
alternatives: A — Dual-key compact: The founding-era compact divides standing authority into a dynastic key (outward dealings, armed defence and watch, declared emergencies, the fortified perimeter) and a council key (allocation of communal stores and labour, dispute-hearing, consent to communal burdens), with a defined dual-key class requiring both keys and newcomer representation through council seat distribution. Displayed, not selected.

B — Presided stewardship: The dynasty presides, speaks outward, and executes what the council resolves but cannot ordinarily spend, allocate, or bind households alone; rotating council stewards hold the working offices and communal stores; the dynasty acts alone only under a declared emergency, every act subject to later council review. Displayed, not selected.

C — Charter-oath assembly: The compact rests on a binding founding oath defining the dynasty's duties (defence, outward dealings, upholding the compact) and limits (no burden without consent, no seizure of households' subsistence, no altering the compact alone); an assembly-chosen council adjudicates oath disputes and holds consent to communal burdens; expertise enters as sworn testimony; newcomer standing follows the household hearth. Selected.
rationale: The selected structure gives both sides genuinely non-ceremonial authority — oath-bounded dynastic breadth against assembly-rooted adjudication and consent — while locating every designed ambiguity exactly where the approaching first succession will bear: on an oath sworn by a living founder who has never needed replacing, whose binding on heirs, receiving body, and disputed terms create contestable process without naming candidates or outcomes.
evidence: Author multiple-choice selection on 2026-08-17 of 'C — Charter-oath assembly', accepting Option C exactly as drafted together with the proposal's shared claim set.
consequences: A standing founder-council compact rests on a binding founding oath the founder swore in the founding era, within the accepted 25-35-years-ago founding range.

The oath defines the dynasty's duties — defence, outward dealings, and upholding the compact — and its limits: no burden without consent, no seizure of households' subsistence, and no altering the compact alone.
The council is chosen by an assembly of the settlement's households and holds two powers: oath adjudication and consent to communal burdens.

Both sides hold real, actually exercised authority; the dynasty's is real and broad within the oath's bounds, the council's is real because it judges those bounds and holds consent, and neither side is merely ceremonial.

Dynasty-side office classes are the oath-bound ruling seat and a sworn deputy class under the same oath; council-assembly-side office classes are an adjudicator class, a burden-consent class, and an oath-witness class whose records are fallible, incomplete, and disputable.

Refugee and newcomer standing follows the household hearth regardless of origin, so newcomer households vote once established, with contested margins over dependents, lodgers, and the not-yet-householded.

Craft, harvest, defence, and System-study expertise enters as sworn testimony in adjudication and burden deliberation; harvest knowledge-holders exist and hold that recognised testimonial standing as the single declared closure of WLD-ECOLOGY-006's open harvest space; System-study testimony interprets accessible signs, never a guaranteed readout.
The compact is a human institution — customary, fallibly recorded, socially enforced — and no office, title, or compact term carries any System-granted power or enforcement.

The ageing founder still rules at story start; the settlement's first succession under the compact is approaching; its provisions are incompletely specified or contested; and its known ambiguity classes — heir binding, receiving body, disputed recollection of terms, and adjudication when the seat itself is party — stay deliberately unresolved as a designed open pressure for WLD-EVENT-001.
Emergency authority, wherever placed, is grounded in the accepted ordinary crisis classes, never in System events.

No name, title text, oath or law-code wording, office count, seat count, quorum, calendar, procedure, enforcement mechanism, property or tenure regime, succession outcome, candidate, faction roster, or fishing or harvest law is selected.
No CAL0 change, party mechanic, pooled capability, guaranteed appraisal, category eligibility, new mechanic, constant, or notification behaviour is created.
residual_unknowns: All in-world names and title wording for the seat, offices, council, assembly, compact, and oath remain open.
The exact first-succession process and its resolution remain open — deliberately unresolved; the ambiguity classes feed WLD-EVENT-001 and must not be settled as background fact.
Assembly-standing margins over dependents, lodgers, and the not-yet-householded, and council size, seat counts, cadence, quorum, and selection procedures remain open.
How sworn expert standing is recognised in practice for craft, harvest, defence, and System-study voices, and how contested that recognition is, remain open.
The compact's record form — what is written, remembered, witnessed, or disputed, and who keeps it — remains open.
Law content of any kind — offences, penalties, tenure, inheritance, water and road arrangements, and every harvest question — remains open.
The compact's history of past emergencies, adjudications, reviews, and precedents remains open.
How returning non-human peoples relate to the outward-dealings duty remains open, with their histories and aims unflattened and undeveloped.
How the compact is known, misunderstood, or mythologised inside and outside the settlement remains open.
reopening_conditions: Later accepted worldbuilding or story evidence cannot support any coherent charter-oath assembly compact within the accepted founding range.
Later accepted governance, law, tenure, or harvest work contradicts the oath-duty and consent structure rather than extending it.
Story development requires a succession resolution that no coherent reading of the compact's ambiguity classes supports.
Later accepted work on the cultural fabric, returning non-human peoples, or crisis classes cannot be reconciled with hearth-standing assembly composition or the emergency grounding.
The Author explicitly chooses another compact structure.
